record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Determine the class of spacetimes that are asymptotically velocity dominated near a singularity, in a suitably defined sense.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Lorentzian spacetime satisfying the Einstein equations (in vacuum or coupled to suitable matter) and possessing a cosmological singularity, e.g. a crushing singularity along which the mean curvature of a foliation by spacelike hypersurfaces blows up. In a neighborhood of such a singularity choose a Gaussian (or constant-mean-curvature) foliation with time coordinate $t\to 0^+$, induced spatial metric $g_{ij}(t,x)$ and second fundamental form $K_{ij}(t,x)$. The Einstein evolution equations on this foliation take the schematic form
$$\partial_t g_{ij} = -2 K_{ij},\qquad \partial_t K^i{}_j = (\text{spatial-curvature terms}) + (\text{velocity terms involving }K)+\text{matter}.$$
The associated "velocity-dominated system" is obtained by deleting all spatial-derivative (curvature) terms from the Einstein equations, leaving an ODE in $t$ at each spatial point $x$. A solution $(g,K)$ is said to be asymptotically velocity dominated (AVD) near the singularity if there exists a solution $(\tilde g,\tilde K)$ of the velocity-dominated system on the same spatial manifold such that, as $t\to 0^+$, suitable rescaled differences $g_{ij}-\tilde g_{ij}$, $K^i{}_j-\tilde K^i{}_j$ (and analogous matter quantities) tend to zero in an appropriate norm, with errors decaying faster than the leading velocity-dominated behavior.

Problem. Give an intrinsic characterization of the class of spacetimes that are asymptotically velocity dominated near a cosmological singularity in this sense. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a precise, geometrically invariant definition of "asymptotically velocity dominated singularity" valid for general (not necessarily symmetric) spacetimes.

(b) Identify necessary and sufficient conditions on the initial data, matter model, and symmetry/structure of the spacetime under which AVD behavior holds at the singularity.

(c) Describe the maximal class of spacetimes within vacuum general relativity, and within Einstein-matter systems (scalar field, stiff fluid, electromagnetic, etc.), whose generic singularities are AVD, distinguishing them from spacetimes exhibiting oscillatory (Mixmaster/BKL) behavior.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization of spacetimes exhibiting asymptotically velocity-dominated (AVTD/AVD) behavior at cosmological singularities is widely regarded as open. AVTD behavior has been rigorously established only for restricted classes (e.g. polarized and general Gowdy spacetimes, polarized $U(1)$-symmetric cosmologies, Einstein-scalar field/stiff fluid systems via Fuchsian methods), but a complete intrinsic classification distinguishing AVD from oscillatory BKL/Mixmaster behavior in generic spacetimes remains an active research question, with recent work continuing on silent wave equations and Iwasawa-frame descriptions.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Approaches to Spacetime Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: The generic singularity in spatially homogeneous cosmologies ... approach to it asymptotically falls into two classes. The first, called asymptotically velocity term dominated (AVTD), refers to a cosmology that approaches the Kasner solution as the singularity is approached.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of AVTD versus oscillatory singular behavior remains a major question in mathematical relativity.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics of Solutions to Silent Wave Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work analyzing asymptotic velocity-dominated behavior via silent wave equations.
status_evidence.claim: AVD behavior is still being actively studied and not fully classified.

status_evidence.title: Velocity dominated singularities in the cheese slice universe
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of AVD behavior in specific inhomogeneous models.
status_evidence.claim: AVD established only in specific classes of spacetimes.

status_evidence.title: Recent Advances in Cosmological Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of current state of singularity classification in cosmology.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of singular behavior in general spacetimes remains incomplete.
